common_misconception_pair.fact: The 180-axis rule establishes an imaginary line between two interacting subjects and keeps all camera setups on one side of that line so screen direction stays consistent (p. 36).

pamphlet_excerpts: Core Filmmaking Fundamentals: Here are some points to consider as you begin shooting your first film (p. 36).
Spatial Scene Orientation: Imagine entering an elevator where two people are already in conversation (p. 36).
Consistent Left-to-Right Eyeline: The individual on your left, a man, is looking to your right (p. 36).
Matching Counterpart Sightline: The other person, a woman, is looking to your left to respond (p. 36).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Establish First Subject Eyeline: The individual on your left, a man, is looking to your right (p. 36).
Step 2 - Match Opposing Subject Gaze: The other person, a woman, is looking to your left to respond (p. 36).
Step 3 - Frame Individual Close-Up Shots: If you were filming this conversation in close-upshots, only one person might be seen speaking at a time (p. 36).
Step 4 - Maintain Consistent Screen Direction: If the man changes the direction he is looking, the audience will be confused as to who is talking (p. 36).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When filming a conversation between two characters on set, why must you maintain the 180-degree axis of action rule as you switch camera setups?
quiz_item.question: When filming a conversation between two characters on set, why must you maintain the 180-degree axis of action rule as you switch camera setups?
options: A. To ensure the camera microphone stays pointed away from background wind noise during outdoor shoots.
B. To keep the shutter speed locked at exactly double the frame rate when panning across a room.
C. To prevent lens flare by keeping the key light directly behind the camera on every shot.
D. To keep both characters looking toward each other on consistent sides of the frame so the audience does not become spatially disoriented when shots are cut together.
choices: A. To ensure the camera microphone stays pointed away from background wind noise during outdoor shoots.
B. To keep the shutter speed locked at exactly double the frame rate when panning across a room.
C. To prevent lens flare by keeping the key light directly behind the camera on every shot.
D. To keep both characters looking toward each other on consistent sides of the frame so the audience does not become spatially disoriented when shots are cut together.
quiz_item.correct_answer: D. To keep both characters looking toward each other on consistent sides of the frame so the audience does not become spatially disoriented when shots are cut together.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Keeping all camera positions on one side of the imaginary 180-degree line of action preserves consistent screen direction and eyelines across cuts.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: When filming a conversation between two characters on set, why must you maintain the 180-degree axis of action rule as you switch camera setups?
options: A. To ensure the camera microphone stays pointed away from background wind noise during outdoor shoots.
B. To keep the shutter speed locked at exactly double the frame rate when panning across a room.
C. To prevent lens flare by keeping the key light directly behind the camera on every shot.
D. To keep both characters looking toward each other on consistent sides of the frame so the audience does not become spatially disoriented when shots are cut together.
choices: A. To ensure the camera microphone stays pointed away from background wind noise during outdoor shoots.
B. To keep the shutter speed locked at exactly double the frame rate when panning across a room.
C. To prevent lens flare by keeping the key light directly behind the camera on every shot.
D. To keep both characters looking toward each other on consistent sides of the frame so the audience does not become spatially disoriented when shots are cut together.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. To keep both characters looking toward each other on consistent sides of the frame so the audience does not become spatially disoriented when shots are cut together.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Keeping all camera positions on one side of the imaginary 180-degree line of action preserves consistent screen direction and eyelines across cuts.

patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Keeping props, wardrobe, and lighting consistent across shots prevents continuity errors that would break the illusion of continuous time when the scene is edited together (p. 28).
